sentences.text: There are three ways to name the same direction, and the whole subject is getting from one to another without losing your way.
Look at the chain on screen.
True is the direction on the chart.
Magnetic is where a perfect compass would point.
Compass is what yours actually reads.
Between true and magnetic sits variation.
Between magnetic and compass sits deviation.
So the order is: true, variation, magnetic, deviation, compass.
Going from compass toward true is called correcting.
When you’re correcting, add easterly errors and subtract westerly ones.
Going the other way, from true down to compass, is uncorrecting, and you do the opposite.
A sentence to remember the correcting order: Can Dead Men Vote Twice At Elections.
Compass, deviation, magnetic, variation, true, add east.
Write that at the top of your scratch paper on exam day, before you read a single question.
